Based on the healthcare Q&A matches, it appears that radiotherapy of the primary rectal cancer can negatively impact prognosis after pelvic exenteration for recurrent rectal cancer. A study found that patients who previously received radiotherapy for primary rectal cancer treatment have worse oncologic outcomes than those who had not received radiotherapy after pelvic exenteration for locally recurrent rectal cancer.

This is because the previous radiotherapy has altered the biology of the disease, making it more resistant to subsequent treatments such as surgery. In other words, the presence of radiotherapy can create a "tumor microenvironment" that makes future treatments less effective.

Therefore, patients who have received radiotherapy for primary rectal cancer and then undergo pelvic exenteration for recurrent rectal cancer may face a poorer prognosis compared to those who did not receive prior radiotherapy.
